correctness.rationale: A projector is uniquely an ordered pair of distinct image and kernel lines, so conjugacy is transitive and fixing E=diag(1,0) costs a factor q(q+1). Cayley–Hamilton characterizes the remaining rank-one idempotents by trace one and determinant zero in every characteristic. Their off-diagonals satisfy xy=A and uv=C, and the third trace equation is xv+yu=d. If AC≠0, s=xv gives s+AC/s=d and each admissible s leaves precisely x∈K× free. If one product is zero the two coordinate-axis branches give 2(q−1) choices for d≠0 and intersect in the unique zero choice for each nonzero factorization when d=0. If both are zero, splitting (x,y) into its two open axes and the origin gives 2(q−1) for d≠0 and 2q(q−1)+(2q−1)=2q²−1 for d=0. In the nondegenerate support, s↦AC/s has one fixed point for even q and 1+χ(AC) for odd q; its orbits are exactly the attainable d values. For odd q the resulting summed bias is (sum_a χ(a(1−a)))²=1, by the difference-of-squares hyperbola count with 2 invertible. All 4(q−1) degenerate (a,c) pairs support all q values of b. These give the stated support for both parities, and the strict inequality 2q²−1>2(q−1) identifies exactly the four maxima, including q=2. An independent exhaustive fixed-E count over orders 4, 8 and 9 matched every cell, support 56, 368 and 509, and exactly four maximum cells in each case.
residual_risks: Uploaded code was inspected, not executed; the independent finite check corroborates rather than replacing the all-field proof. Trace fibers are not claimed to separate triple conjugacy orbits.

evidence: Projector P is (im P, ker P), an ordered pair of projective-line points. For nondegenerate E,F the cross-ratio may be chosen as (a−1)/a where a=tr(EF); swapping one ordered pair inverts that cross-ratio and sends a to 1−a. Hollmann–Xiang Definition 4.2 takes the set {r,r^{-1}} on hyperbolic secants. For odd q, X=2P−I instead gives a fixed-norm traceless vector with polar pairing tr(XY)/2=2tr(PQ)−1.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These identify both the ordered orbital formulation and the standard orthogonal Gram formulation. The trace relation alone is not a coherent-configuration relation system at 0 and 1: it merges complementary or identical projections with other shared-line configurations. The frozen count sums over such distinctions without fusing a with 1−a.
